metadata.title: Chris Bell Remains a Stash-Worthy Waiver Option
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Chris Bell officially caught zero passes in a Week 4 loss to the Vikings, but his day almost looked much different from a fantasy perspective. Bell had a 68-yard touchdown wiped off the board by an illegal touch penalty that came down to a fraction of an inch. While results have been inconsistent, Bell's usage has been on the rise after missing most of training camp while rehabbing the ACL tear that ended his collegiate career. He saw a season-high 82% snap share in Week 4, his second straight game topping 70%, and while the Dolphins passing offense is unlikely to support multiple fantasy options, Bell has the talent to emerge as the Miami receiver to roster, particularly if his snap counts keep rising.

metadata.title: Chris Bell catchless in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Chris Bell did not bring in any of his three targets in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: The rookie had one big touchdown that got called back due to penalty, and outside of that, he wasn't able to do anything at all. He didn't catch any of his three targets and ended up with a goose egg for fantasy purposes. He should not be started moving forward, even if he has enough talent to break out at some point in the season.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Can Be a Deep-League Option in Week 4
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell stepped up last week with Caleb Douglas (ankle) out, and he's set for a substantial role in Week 4 against the Vikings while Douglas misses a second straight contest. Bell set season highs in snaps, routes, and targets last Sunday, catching four of his seven targets for 67 yards. He was limited by a knee issue this week as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he sustained in November, but he does not have an injury designation this week, meaning he should be good to go as the team's second receiver behind Malik Washington. The rookie brings good upside with volume available, although the overall struggles of the Dolphins' offense led by QB Malik Willis do cap his ceiling. Bell is the WR53 in RotoBaller's rankings for Week 4, and he's definitely emerging as a deep-league option to consider. With bye weeks around the corner, he's also an important option to watch as a potential depth pickup in standard-sized leagues.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Clear for Sunday
metadata.description: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: With Caleb Douglas (ankle) already ruled out for Miami, Bell appears set to remain a big part of the passing offense after he set season highs in snaps, routes and targets last Sunday against Kansas City. In Miami's offense that struggles to score points coupled with Minnesota's strong defense, Bell is difficult to trust for fantasy lineups.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) will play Sunday
metadata.description: Chris Bell (knee) will play in Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
metadata.analysis: The rookie is going to be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed on Miami's injury report due to a knee issue of some kind. He will be primed for a lot of work with Caleb Douglas (ankle) already ruled out ahead of Week 4's matchup against the Vikings.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Chris Bell (knee) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday as the team continues to limit his workload at practice. He should be available to play this week, however, and will be primed for more work than usual with Caleb Douglas (ankle) trending towards missing another game.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Reps capped again
metadata.description: Bell (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: The Dolphins kept Bell's reps in check for the second day in a row, but the team hasn't indicated that he's dealing with a setback with his surgically repaired right knee. As long as he can practice in some fashion Friday, Bell should be in good position to suit up Sunday against the Vikings. Through his first three NFL games, the rookie third-round pick out of Louisville has put together a 5-92-0 receiving line on 11 targets.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) listed as limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Chris Bell (knee) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was limited to start the practice week on Wednesday due to a knee issue. It seems unlikely to affect his availability for Week 4, however, and he seems primed to see more work against the Vikings with Caleb Douglas (ankle) trending towards missing another game for Miami.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Bell (knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: Notably, Caleb Douglas (ankle) was absent from Wednesday's practice, which could allow Bell to play an increased role again in Week 4 after he caught four of seven targets for 67 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Chiefs. Bell has been seeing his practice reps managed all summer after undergoing ACL surgery late last season.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Sees increased snaps in Week 3
metadata.description: Bell caught four of seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: With Caleb Douglas (ankle) inactive and De'Von Achane suffering a torn ACL in the first half against Kanas City, Bell was one of the biggest beneficiaries from both a playing time and opportunity perspective. His seven targets were tied for second on the team with Greg Dulcich behind Malik Washington's 10. If Douglas needs to miss more time, Bell could again see elevated snaps Sunday against Minnesota.

metadata.title: Chris Bell a Waiver-Wire Candidate After Encouraging Week 3 Performance
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Chris Bell had the best game of his young career in his team's Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, recording four catches for 67 yards on seven targets. With fellow Dolphins rookie wideout Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined by an ankle injury, Bell emerged as a key target for Miami quarterback Malik Willis. Bell played on 71% of Miami's offensive snaps on Sunday and finished tied for second on the team in targets. Douglas' eventual return could impact Bell's playing time. However, the 22-year-old is only getting healthier himself after missing a large chunk of the summer while recovering from a torn ACL. As Bell gets more comfortable in terms of both health and experience, his production could continue to improve. In PPR-scoring leagues with 12 or more teams, Bell profiles as a worthy waiver wire target for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Chris Bell leads pass-catchers in Week 3 loss to Chiefs
metadata.description: Chris Bell hauled in four of his seven targets for 67 yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Bell found a way to make an impact, finishing with more than one reception for the first time in three contests Sunday. The wideout remains one of many pass-catchers difficult to trust in the Dolphins offense early on, with a Week 4 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Set Up for an Increased Role in Week 3
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell is in position to pick up more work in his team's home opener this week against the Chiefs. His fellow rookie Caleb Douglas (ankle) is out for this matchup, leaving Bell more opportunities to step up across the field from veteran Malik Washington. Bell was dealing with soreness and fluid buildup in his surgically repaired left knee earlier this week, but does not have an injury designation and should be good to go against the Chiefs. Kansas City has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points to WRs this year, which sets Bell up in a tough spot even if he does take on a larger workload. He didn't have a catch last week after catching one of two targets against the Raiders for 25 yards. The Dolphins' passing game has struggled early in the year, making Bell tough to trust even in a bigger role. He does have boom-or-bust potential, but he is only RotoBaller's WR78 this week, making him best left on the bench or the waiver wire for Week 3 in most leagues.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Chris Bell (knee) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: The rookie will be available to play on Sunday after being limited at practice earlier in the week due to a knee issue of some kind. Expect him to see even more work with Caleb Douglas (ankle) set to be sidelined against the Chiefs this week.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Good to go for Week 3
metadata.description: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: With fellow rookie wideout Caleb Douglas (ankle) ruled out, Bell took on a larger role in Miami's passing game despite recently dealing with fluid buildup and soreness in his surgically repaired right knee. Doctors told him it isn't a major concern, and Bell then told reporters Thursday that he plans to play Week 3.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Likely to Play in Week 3
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Chris Bell (knee) is likely to play on Sunday in Week 3 against the visiting Kansas City Chiefs, according to Alain Poupart of Sports Illustrated. Meanwhile, fellow rookie Caleb Douglas (ankle) has already been ruled out for the weekend. It means that if Bell suits up, as expected, he should have a much bigger role as the Dolphins seek to pull off a huge upset in Miami. The 22-year-old has experienced some fluid buildup in his surgically repaired left knee, but he has been told it is nothing serious. The Dolphins eased him into practice reps this week as a precaution, but he is expected to be active on Sunday. The third-rounder from Louisville has had a slow start to his NFL career with the Dolphins, catching just one of his three targets for 25 yards without a trip to the end zone. With Douglas out, Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington might be quarterback Malik Willis' top targets. Bell should see more snaps as well, but he is much too risky to use in most starting fantasy lineups in Week 3.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) plans to play Sunday
metadata.description: Chris Bell (knee) told reporters that he plans to play in Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: The rookie is dealing with a knee issue right now, but it's not considered a serious issue, and he told reporters that he is planning to play through it against the Chiefs. It remains to be seen if he will carry an injury designation heading into the weekend, but it looks highly likely that the team will clear him to play sooner rather than later.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Intends to play Sunday
metadata.description: Bell (knee) said Thursday that he'll be ready to play Sunday against the Chiefs, C. C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Bell said that he's experiencing some fluid buildup and soreness in his surgically repaired left knee, though doctors told him that it was nothing worrisome. The Dolphins have still been managing the rookie receiver carefully this week nonetheless, as he was a limited participant in Wednesday's session and was spotted working off to the side during the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, according to David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel. Though Bell is tracking to suit up Sunday, he may need to practice fully Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) practices off to side Thursday
metadata.description: Chris Bell was seen practicing off to the side on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Bell was officially limited in practice on Wednesday. His status will need to be monitored in Thursday's injury report.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Working on side Thursday
metadata.description: Bell (knee) "mostly worked on the side" during the media-viewing portion of Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: After being listed as a limited participant Wednesday, Bell appears to have taken a step back Thursday, assuming he indeed goes down as a non-participant on Thursday's practice report. Fellow rookie third-round pick Caleb Douglas (ankle) also wasn't spotted Thursday, leaving Miami banged up at wide receiver behind de facto top option Malik Washington ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Chiefs.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Dealing with knee injury
metadata.description: Bell was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: Per C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald, Bell was spotted working out off to the side during the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice. The Dolphins haven't revealed whether Bell's limitations to begin Week 3 prep are related to the torn ACL he suffered last December, but he'll now have two more practices to prove his health this week ahead of Sunday's contest against the Chiefs. Through two games to begin his career, the rookie third-round pick has tallied one catch (on three targets) for 25 yards.

metadata.title: Chris Bell (knee) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Chris Bell was limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Bell opens the week on the injury report with a knee issue. He remains in a limited role right now in the Dolphins offense.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Catchless in second pro game
metadata.description: Bell did not catch his only target Sunday in a Week 2 loss to San Francisco.
metadata.analysis: Bell was unable to make an impact, but that was in line with most of Miami's passing game, as QB Malik Willis threw for only 120 yards outside of a 77-yard touchdown to Ryan Miller during garbage time. Bell logged 24 of the Dolphins' 59 offensive snaps, ranking a distant third among team's wideouts behind Malik Washington (55) and Caleb Douglas (51). Douglas suffered an ankle injury late in the contest, however, and he's uncertain to be able to suit up in Week 3 against Kansas City. If he ends up being sidelined, Bell could move up a notch in the WR pecking order.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Yet To Show Off Potential In First Two Weeks
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell was held without a catch on one target in the team's Week 2 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The rookie receiver out of Louisville has yet to display his potential thought the first two weeks of the season and really hasn't been looked for all that much by quarterback Malik Willis. Bell was a third round pick in the 2026 draft so he clearly has some potential. At 6-foot-2 and 220 pounds he is on the larger side for a wide receiver. He had one catch for 25 yards on two targets in Week 1 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Bell has an opportunity in what is a fairly thin wide receiver room with the Dolphins. Look for him to establish himself in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Until we see something from Bell, though, he has to be left on the waiver wire aside from very deep leagues or keeper leagues.

metadata.title: Chris Bell a non-factor in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Chris Bell failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Bell gained 25 yards on his only catch in Week 1, but through two games, the rookie has gotten just three total targets from QB Malik Willis. Bell may merit stash status in dynasty formats, but he's off the redraft radar at the moment.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Brings Intriguing Potential, Hard to Start in Week 2
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell has quickly emerged as a starting option for the team after recovering from his ACL tear, which he suffered last December while at Louisville. Bell operated as the team's third receiver and caught one of his two targets for 25 yards in the team's Week 1 loss to the Raiders. He played 52% of the team's offensive snaps, well behind Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas but well ahead of fourth receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. He has intriguing long-term potential this season since he's quickly risen to such a big role, but he's only the No. 79 WR in RotoBaller's Week 2 rankings, so he shouldn't be in starting lineups just yet. He's a solid bench stash for deep leagues, but still needs to show more before you can count on him regularly.

metadata.title: Chris Bell - Hauls in 25-yard catch in NFL debut
metadata.description: Bell caught one pass on two targets for 25 yards during the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: It wasn't until the third quarter that Bell logged his first NFL catch, hauling in 25-yard pass from Malik Willis to keep the drive going and ending with a 14-yard touchdown run by the latter two plays later. The rookie wideout saw the field for 29 of the Dolphins' 56 offensive snaps (51.2 percent), which was third-most among Miami's wide receivers behind Malik Washington (55) and fellow rookie Caleb Douglas (51). It was encouraging to see Bell on the field, seeing as he tore his ACL last December, and his snap count should steadily increase as his conditioning improves. Bell and the Dolphins face a tough Week 2 matchup Sept. 20, against a 49ers defense that limited league MVP Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense to just seven points Week 1.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Could Emerge as Stash Option
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell made his NFL debut against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The Dolphins selected Bell in the third round during this year's draft. He's expected to be a significant part of the offense during his first year in Miami. On Sunday, Bell got off to a slow start as he didn't record his first catch until the third quarter. He finished the day, hauling in one 25-yard pass on three targets in the loss to the Raiders. The good news is that Bell played over 50 percent of the offensive snaps on Sunday. He didn't make a ton of noise in his debut, but it sounds like he's going to see steady playing time. Fantasy managers in deep leagues should consider stashing Bell for later in the season. He'll get a tough test against the San Francisco 49ers defense in Week 2.

metadata.title: Chris Bell catches one pass in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Chris Bell caught one of his two targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Bell made the most of minimal involvement in an underwhelming Miami air attack, highlighted by a 25-yard reception in the loss. The wideout remains difficult to trust as part of a Miami offense still establishing their identity under new head coach Jeff Hafley, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

metadata.title: Chris Bell Has the Potential to Emerge in Miami's Offense
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell was named as one of the team's starting receivers in his NFL debut in Week 1 against the Las Vegas Raiders. An ACL tear ended his college career at Louisville and caused him to slide to the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Even though he missed most of his first training camp while rehabbing, he has made a splash right away with a quick acclimation to the Dolphins' offense. He only played one preseason game, but he was targeted five times in about 10 minutes of game action. In Week 1, Bell is RotoBaller's WR73, just behind teammates Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington. Bell could end up being the top fantasy receiver in Miami's offense at some point this season, and he has a huge opportunity ahead of him. He's extremely high risk for Week 1, but he's a rookie to monitor moving forward.
